statement: A logical relation is not its row, column, file, object or memory representation.
A declarative query is not a logical plan, physical plan, execution attempt or result occurrence.
Logical operators and physical algorithms must not collapse.
Successful parsing or serialization does not establish binding, meaning or executability.
Lower estimated cost does not prove semantic equivalence or lower realized cost.
Cardinality and cost estimates are not observed cardinalities or resource facts.
Set, bag/multiset and ordered sequence semantics must remain distinct.
A row occurrence is not automatically a business entity or event.
A physical column is not automatically one logical attribute or semantic measure.
Null, unknown, absent, inapplicable, empty and numerical zero must not collapse.
SQL unknown is not Boolean false.
Equality, not-distinct, ordering equality, hash equality and identity are separate relations.
Collation equality/order is not byte equality/order.
NaN and null are different partiality/value states.
A result without a complete ordering key has no stable row order guarantee.
LIMIT without a total order is not deterministic top-N.
A partial sort key does not decide order among ties.
Equal function names do not imply equal null, error, volatility, numerical or timezone semantics.
Deterministic for one invocation is not immutable across data, session or edition changes.
A SQL aggregate is not a governed business measure definition.
A data cube is an analytical algebra/result space, not a vendor product or lakehouse.
An OLAP dimension is not merely a table named dimension.
A dimension hierarchy is not generic sort order or arbitrary parent-child edges.
Roll-up is not universally SUM and is invalid when grain/hierarchy/measure summarizability fails.
Analytical grain is not row count.
A measure additive over one dimension is not necessarily additive over all dimensions.
A subtotal cell and a detail row remain different semantic occurrences even when values coincide.
Syntactic similarity is not query equivalence.
A provider accepting a rewritten plan does not prove semantic preservation.
Catalog/table statistics are scoped observations or estimates, not timeless truth.
Ordering, partitioning, locality and vector width are physical properties unless explicitly visible in the result contract.
Parquet/Arrow files or batches are not tables, snapshots, transactions or catalogs.
Table-format state and catalog authority are separate bounded contexts.
A bound snapshot/version is not the moving notion of latest.
Snapshot isolation and serializability must not collapse.
Statement and transaction snapshot cuts must not collapse.
Independent source snapshots do not automatically form one globally consistent federated cut.
A connector's general feature support is not proof that a particular invocation was lossless or guaranteed.
Pushdown is an optimization only when translated semantics plus residual equal the original operation.
An omitted residual is not evidence that translation was complete.
Virtual relation, materialized view, result cache and exported dataset identities must remain distinct.
A cache hit is not proof of freshness, authorization equivalence or snapshot equivalence.
Arrow/Substrait/Parquet representation compatibility does not imply semantic compatibility.
A successful kernel call does not prove the requested null, error, precision or determinism contract.
Shuffle/capture may destroy order; distribution equality is not sequence equality.
Parallel execution may preserve relational results while changing order, timing and floating-point reduction outcomes.
Adaptive execution may change physical strategy but must not silently change query meaning.
Successful spill does not establish bounded latency, confidentiality or durable result completion.
Admission, scheduling, execution start, execution completion and result delivery are distinct states.
Query completion is not export delivery, publication, downstream adoption or business outcome.
A query receipt is bounded execution evidence, not proof that inputs or business semantics were correct.
Benchmark performance is not semantic conformance or fitness for unrelated workloads.
TPC-H/TPC-DS performance does not establish universal performance, cost, reliability or scale.
A managed warehouse experience is not the query engine, table format, catalog or resource substrate it composes.
Lakehouse is an architecture pattern; a suite may package products but does not become one semantic owner.
An open table format alone is not a lakehouse.
Lakehouse and warehouse packaging must not erase independent table, catalog, query, maintenance, sharing and governance contracts.
AI or agents may propose queries/plans but cannot infer hidden grain, choose semantic defaults, waive residuals or authorize effects.
